procedure: Stop and inventory: `git status`, `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`. Note whether this is a merge, rebase or cherry-pick (`git status` says).

Learn both sides' intent before touching code: read claude/sessions/*.json from both branches (`git show <other-branch>:claude/sessions/` lists them), then `git log --oneline --left-right HEAD...MERGE_HEAD -- <path>` per conflicted file.
Apply the matching rule below for each path (first matching `path` glob wins). Paths with no rule: merge by hand, keeping both sides' behavior.
Never blanket `git checkout --ours/--theirs .` on source files. It silently drops a teammate's work.
Regenerate generated files (lockfile, build info) instead of hand-merging them.

After resolving: `grep -rn '^<<<<<<<\|^>>>>>>>' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.css' --include='*.json' --include='*.sql' --include='*.md' .` must be empty (skip node_modules), then `npm run typecheck && npm run lint`.
If intent is unclear or both sides changed the same behavior in incompatible ways, ask the human. Don't guess on design direction.
Record what you did and why in your session file's `conflict_notes`. If the resolution generalizes, add a rule here.
revert_safety: This repo has had revert-of-revert cycles (warm redesign: #4, #6, #9, #10). Before merging any branch whose name or commits mention revert/restore, check `git log --oneline main..<branch>` and confirm with the human which state is wanted.
Reverting a merge commit means later re-merging the same branch silently brings nothing. To restore it, revert the revert; don't re-merge.

rules.how: Session files are one per session and should never conflict. If two have the same name, rename one (append -2) and keep both. Never merge contents.

Treat as a JSON object. Union arrays (dedupe exact strings). For scalar conflicts, keep the side whose change is newer per git log, unless the other side records a fact the newer side contradicts by mistake. Set `updated` to today. Validate with `node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('claude/project.json'))"`.
Union `procedure`, `revert_safety` and `rules` (dedupe rules by `path`, merging their `how` text). Set `updated`. Validate JSON.

Resolve package.json first, then `git checkout --theirs package-lock.json` (or ours, whichever matches the base you're landing on) and run `npm install` to regenerate. Commit the result. Never hand-edit.
Keep every dependency and script from both sides. For the same package at different versions, take the higher semver unless a session file says a pin was deliberate.
The nextjs-agent-rules block is generated by `next dev`. Take either side; it gets rewritten. Keep any hand-written text outside the BEGIN/END markers from both sides.
Generated and gitignored. `git rm --cached tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` if it shows up.
Generated and gitignored. `git rm --cached next-env.d.ts` if tracked.

Theme tokens. Current direction is the warm redesign (project.json design.current). Keep token ADDITIONS from both sides. On a value conflict for the same token, prefer the warm-palette side; never reintroduce neon hex values (#22D3EE, #A78BFA, #F472B6, ...) unless the human says the design changed. Check both :root (dark) and the light-theme block; every --hue-* key must exist in both.

Branch `color` replaced NEON with HUES + hueVar/interestColor/identityColor/preferredHue. If the other side still imports NEON or adds code using raw hex from it, keep HUES and port their usages: group color → the hue from lib/client/groupHues.ts; interest color → interestColor(id); person → identityColor(user). Keep hashString and rgba.
Deleted by the warm redesign (Ambient is now static paper grain). If the other side modified it, keep it deleted and ask the human whether that change matters.

Merge logic by hand. Common pattern: one side changed colors (hex → hueVar/useHueHex), the other changed behavior. Keep the behavior change and re-apply the color change on top of it. No hardcoded hex in components.

Keep every table/column from both sides. Make sure scripts/migrate.ts --upgrade adds each new column idempotently for existing databases, and that lib/store/types.ts, memory.ts and oracle.ts all reflect it. Never resolve by running --reset on the shared DB.
Keep both sides' methods. After merging, types.ts, memory.ts and oracle.ts must agree; typecheck enforces the interface.
Keep both sides' people/groups/friendships. Ensure ids and group names stay unique (case-insensitive) and friendship pairs are ordered/unique.
Keep both sides' text. If they disagree, the newer decision wins and the older one gets marked superseded rather than deleted.
